title: 1967 AHSME Problem 7
statement: If \(\dfrac ab\lt-\dfrac cd,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d\) are real numbers and \(bd\ne0,\) then:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: \(a\) can be negative or zero, but not positive

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(a\) can be positive, negative, or zero

solutions.text:
Take \(b=d=1\) and \(c=-2.\) The inequality becomes \(a\lt2,\) which is satisfied by positive, zero, and negative values of \(a.\) Thus none of the three possible signs is forced.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: The signs of \(b,c,d\) are unrestricted except that \(b,d\ne0\)
Try \(b=d=1\) and choose \(c\) so that the right side is positive
